title: add known_pseudo_classes to the codebase to prevent unnecessary invalidations on :global and :local
author: calebdwilliams
summary: Adds a public `knownPseudoClasses` option (ParserOptions, MinifyOptions, napi, C, TS types, docs) so unknown pseudo-classes like `:global`/`:local` are treated as compatible and don't trigger `:is()` wrapping. The author's use case is running Lightning CSS without CSS modules on CSS that still contains `:global()` for a later tool, i.e. non-standard syntax that per project policy should be processed first. The maintainer instead pointed at a real bug (a no-op visitor causes the wrapping in CSS-modules mode, #1079) to debug, and the option is new public API that also changes ParserOptions/MinifyOptions struct literals (breaking for Rust users).
evidence: devongovett 2026-05-17: 'this seems to have more to do with there being a visitor than the `:global` pseudo alone ... (turn off the visitor and it seems right). Seems like we should debug that.' zslabs posted a CSS-modules + no-op visitor repro on 2026-08-17. CLAUDE.md: 'Other syntax extensions are not supported ... external tools should process them first.' #1079 (visitor-induced :is() wrapping) is still open with no fix PR.
draft:
Thanks for the PR, and sorry for the slow reply. I don't think we want a separate option for this. `:global`/`:local` are CSS modules syntax, so when CSS modules aren't enabled in Lightning CSS, the best approach is to run the CSS modules step first, or enable `cssModules` here so they're compiled away before minifying.

The case that does look like a real bug is the one in #1079: with CSS modules enabled, a visitor that returns the rule unchanged still causes the selector list to be wrapped in `:is()`. That should be fixed at its source rather than worked around with a list of known pseudo-classes, so I'm going to close this in favor of tracking that in #1079. Thanks again for digging into it!
